findings.title: Win-overlay Close desyncs won from board state; persist() saves a finished board that restores as a broken empty table
findings.detail: Close sets game.won=false directly from the view without resetting/redealing the board. persist()'s only guard is !won, so backgrounding after Close writes the fully-solved empty board to causeway.game; on relaunch restore() passes its 52-card count check (cards are on foundations) and restores won=false with nothing to tap and no win banner. Deterministically reachable. Web derives completion via isWon() so has no equivalent.

status_history.note: found via code trace; persist() guard added in 770b422 interacts badly with pre-existing Close handler

findings.title: isSeqHead unbounded-index crash (R1) fixed on iOS only - web still crashes on the same race
findings.location: index.html isSeqHead (~419-435), called from smartMove and handleCardTap
findings.detail: iOS isSeqHead was bounds-guarded per REVIEW-2 R1; the web function was never given the same guard. Node repro: stale idx past a column shortened by an intervening autoplay pop throws TypeError reading 'color'. Web autoplay uses setTimeout gaps in which a dblclick/click racing a re-render can deliver a stale {col,idx}. BACKLOG R1 claim of 'both platforms' is only true for iOS.

status_history.note: reproduced with a standalone Node harness

findings.title: Restore sanity check validates card count only, not validity/uniqueness or foundation legality
findings.detail: Check is inTableau+inCells+onFoundations==52 arithmetic only. 52 copies of an invalid/duplicate card pass; crossed up/down pairs can still sum to 52. Not exploitable via UI (only valid decks written) but BACKLOG 'sanity-checks all 52 cards' overstates the guarantee.

status_history.note: verified with a standalone Swift Codable round-trip test

findings.title: Restoring a saved game never resumes autoplay, both platforms
findings.detail: persist/saveGame runs after every autoplayOneStep, so a kill mid-autoplay-chain can persist a board with further safe-autoplayable cards. Neither restore path calls runAutoplay/step, so those cards sit inert until the next manual move. Cosmetic/UX gap.

status_history.note: confirmed by tracing restore bodies on both platforms

findings.title: Privacy policy doesn't mention the new in-progress-game persistence
findings.detail: Lists only settings and solved deal numbers; this commit added the full in-progress board snapshot (causeway.game). Not a privacy risk (on-device only, wiped on delete) but the disclosure is stale.
